  • Now, in a new interview with The Game Business, brand producer Loïc Gounon has expressed much broader ambitions for the character, perhaps bringing Rayman more in line with something like Sonic in terms of visibility.
  • It has been revealed that in other words, Gounon is thinking about not only games, but other mediums too, including TV highlights and comics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ubisoft is gearing up to launch Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 original. While many have questioned the decision to remake a game that arguably still looks and plays great to this day, the developers have been clear in their intention to use Retold as a launchpad for the future of the franchise.

Now, in a new interview with The Game Business, brand producer Loïc Gounon has expressed much broader ambitions for the character, perhaps bringing Rayman more in line with something like Sonic in terms of visibility.

It has been revealed that in other words, Gounon is thinking about not only games, but other mediums too, including TV highlights and comics. The first step is to ensure the brand's success in regions such as the US and Asia, with previous Rayman titles' success being largely limited to Europe.

“I would like to see Rayman as a must-have IP for video games across the world. Rayman was generally stronger in France and the UK, and in some cases in the US. Enlarging the reach of the IP, also towards Asia and performing well in the US, is the first ambition… making sure that we are a must-have platforming adventure title across those markets in the video game world.

“And I guess beyond the video game world. So, comics, TV series... actually, there’s a French comic book that came out with Rabbids and Rayman being reconnected.”.

According to recent reports, however, Gounon does not necessarily believe that producing a upcoming 3D title is the key to success, and instead wants to focus on the characters and lore. Sorry to those hoping for Rayman 4 – hey, it might still happen!

It has been revealed that “Rayman is iconic because of its gameplay. But going back to the adventure roots of Rayman, having people dive into those characters, exploring deeper into that world and mythology, that’s what we believe in.

“It’s the world-building part, the consistency of that world-building, and the empathy for those characters, that will make the franchise last and maybe become bigger.”.

In a recent development, rayman Legends Retold is right around the corner, scheduled to launch on 3rd December 2026. Meanwhile, Ubisoft itself is at the moment coming under fire for its heavy focus on generative AI, with a new report revealing that employees are required to justify reasons for not using the technology in new project pitches.

Would you like to see Rayman become a substantial, successful brand in the future? Or is Ubisoft getting in the way of itself? Let us know with a comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, my Jason gets up at 7am every morning in GTA 6 and sips a cup of coffee while chatting with Lucia. Then he eats an apple, wanders onto the deck to work out, and comes back inside for a quick shower before plotting out his day. You've gotta be realistic, of course. There's no way he can make time to dive for Kenton's treasures and take on that next job with Donnie in an afternoon. But maybe there's time to swing by that fishing spot Cal mentioned and still get home in time to enjoy a few more scenes of domestic bliss.

Sources indicate that I spent my first 20 or so hours playing GTA 6 like it was Stardew Valley rather than an action-packed crime epic, but that's OK by me, as I love the rhythm taking each fresh in-game day as its own little challenge. One night, scrolling social media while cuddled up with Lucia, I ran across a pilot looking for help up north, miles outside of Vice City. It'd be an all-day trip getting up there, but Jason had just gotten into meditation, and Lucia had mentioned a spot out on the edge of the swamp where he might be able to clear his head. Two birds with one stone.

After the usual morning routine, I hopped in the car and headed north, first toward that meditation spot. Surrounded by wildlife, this is the point where I realized you could use the binoculars to look around and study animals to add to the in-game compendium, and I spent more time than I care to admit simply enjoying the sights of the swamp and birdwatching. Oh, a great blue heron? Absolutely majestic.

Industry observers note that I almost had time left to make it up to that pilot job, but I got distracted by an abandoned dinosaur-themed minigolf course on the roadside. I spent hours trying to perfect each hole. By the time I realized how late it had gotten, the sun was already getting low. The twilight put one thought in my mind: "Shit, I'd better get home so I can hang out with Lucia before she goes to sleep.".

But my Jason, clearly awakened to the power of nature by his birdwatching experience, ended up having greater duties than that of a wife guy. Along one of the winding roads that led back home, I heard such a commotion that I had to investigate – a prize pageant cow named Tootsie had escaped from her owner's trailer and was making a break for it.

According to recent reports, I headed her off with my car and got out to calmly talk her down, but as she finally settled I heard the words "save me" echoing in Jason's mind. Leading her back to the trailer, the owner is very grateful – even as he warns that Tootsie is destined for the slaughterhouse after her final run of highlights. At this point, I realized who Jason was becoming. I let Tootsie run free, and when her owner got mad about it, I punched him in the face and stole his cowboy hat as he ran to his truck and drove away.

According to recent reports, that alone might be enough to turn Jason into a hero of the animal rights movement, but the day was not yet done. As darkness settled in on the journey home, I was cruising along the highway on the outskirts of Vice City when I ran into a traffic jam. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.
  • Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.
  • "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries mentioned. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves.".

Game writer Michael Wiafe noted Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

Industry observers note that "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them.".

Sources indicate that fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it.".

GTA 6 rolled out on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2.
  • Originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg.
  • Recent findings suggest that "This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam).

Industry observers note that prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

Originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

Recent findings suggest that "This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent firm Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

It’s all subjective, of course, but Japan’s PS Plus Essential revision for December 2026 looks a little bit better than what we’re getting in the west.

Industry observers note that now if we’re looking at pure value here, the Japanese lineup is objectively better: the Bleach game retails for $59.99, while Amnesia is $24.99. The former is also available on PS5 and PS4, whereas the latter is only available for PS4 (although you can of course play it on PS5 via backwards compatibility).

Bleach is also newer, having released in 2025, while Amnesia is from 2023.

But it does ultimately all come down to taste, I suppose; survival horror fans may be much happier with Frictional’s title – especially if they have no real interest in anime. I suppose the lineup in Japan does lack variety, as you’re getting two very similar titles from Bandai Namco there.

Amnesia: The Bunker did release in Japan, so I’m not entirely sure why the lineup is different between regions.

It has been revealed that sony is putting a lot of marketing into its domestic region at the moment, as it tries to reverse its flagging fortunes. It’s also just launched a newly introduced PS Portal there, and is putting a pretty substantial promotional campaign behind it. Maybe it thinks this lineup will be more enticing to Japanese players.

Industry observers note that interesting stuff, though, which selection would you have preferred? I’ve had the Bleach game on my wishlist for a little while, so I think I would have rather got that – but I can certainly see why people would prefer the more varied worldwide selection as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week, amidst ongoing service disruptions, the US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, claims it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure.".

Sources indicate that finCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone.

Corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X. "As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music.".

A DOGE appointee who previously raised cybersecurity concerns at the IRS with an API "hackathon" and sought to cancel engineering efforts intended to modernize its systems, Corcos is hosting his little LLM project on Github. It's called Legatum, and he describes it as "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization.".

As Corcos writes in its readme, Legatum is "largely" built with the use of AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated. While FinCEN addresses its cybersecurity breach, Corcos and his Claude agents have been steadily pushing updates: At time of writing, the latest commit—added just six minutes ago—tweaked some of its AI art.

Among the other half-dozen or so commits in the last three hours are adjustments to map generation, music updates, and—let's see—attempts at stemming "a wave of political issues and README vandalism" left by Github customers.

That automated moderation evidently still needs some optimizing, judging from the repo's Glitch #220, which reads: "Lead developer is a giant asshole." Another issue notes that "late game American civilization feels broken," because "when you get the Large Language Model tech unlocked, it pretty much destroys any chance of a cultural victory because all your artists are gone, and all your government buildings become totally useless.".

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

FinCEN isn't the only US government organization suffering cybersecurity issues this week. Yesterday, The Fresh York Times reported that the CIA, the Office of the Director of National Security, and the Department of Defense's National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency had been impacted by a vulnerability in an open source intelligence system, which exposed unclassified information.

Industry observers note that on X, Corcos has addressed the questionable optics of overseeing a vibecoded Civ knockoff while his department's facing a cybersecurity intrusion: "Just a heads up, the computers are doing it on their own," Corcos remarked in a reply to a user who compared the incident to Nero fiddling while Rome burned. "Mostly Opus 5.5 orchestrating a bunch of iterative loops.".

In another reply to a more sympathetic user, Corcos was more enthusiastic: "These tools are getting so good it's blowing my mind. A brief voice note on my phone can kick off an amount of work that would have taken dozens of people weeks to deliver," he mentioned. "So cool.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 leaker or leakers Cyberleek claim to to have released the main executable file for an alleged Xbox build of the game that they asserted they'd lobbed onto the net last week. In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.

It has been revealed that referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects". As of writing, the legitimacy of the executable doesn't appear to have been independently verified, meaning it could still just turn out to be a pile of malware or something similarly dodgy. Needless to say, given that and the fact software piracy is illegal, not touching it - or any of the other files Cyberleek claim to have posted - with a barge pole is the sensible thing to do.

Cyberleek have been bigging up the idea that these files they've been releasing could result in GTA 6 running on PC sharpish, via a modified version cobbled together with generative AI. That might happen, but I'm seriously skeptical that if it were to, it wouldn't just be dodgy jankware than runs like piss, rather than anything that'd compare remotely well to an official PC port.

Thus far, it appears a group of would-be recompilers going by Project Leonida may have got the game to start booting on PC, but they since look to have disappeared and scrubbed their established online presence.

All of this again raises the question of whether the threat of any sort of bodged PC recreation coming out of this alleged executable release may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between this month's console release and its eventual Windows release, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year.

Returning to Cyberleek's latest statement, the leaker or leakers have also taken the opportunity to insist that their attempts to pump up a crypto coin as part of the leaking is just for practical reasons rather than grifty ones, honest. "Every donation is a vote for more of this," they wrote. "Where the votes go, [Cyberleek] follows. Crypto here is just a tool - there is no other way to move funds without names.".

It has been revealed that rockstar called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking". Along with parent tech giant Take-Two, they began a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August, but that doesn't seem to to have deterred Cyberleek, if indeed the people leaking under the name are still the same ones as in the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, go big or go home. Playground Games is pushing to make Fable 4 the largest installment of the RPG series to date, at least in terms of the amount of dialog. According to the devs, there are tens of thousands of lines of dialogue, recorded in accents spanning the length and breadth of the British Isles.

Industry observers note that ralph Fulton, the general manager of Fable and co-founder of Playground Games, explains what's gone into the voice-acting with GamesIndustry.biz. "Over a hundred voice actors from all over the UK have contributed to the game, recording over 150,000 lines of dialogue," he says. "It's a mammoth operation.".

Industry observers note that that's a hefty cast, and a considerable amount of scripting. For comparison, Skyrim has around 60,000 lines of spoken dialogue, and Mass Effect contains around 40,000. Those are significant RPGs, with a lot of characters to meet and chat to.

Fallout 4 is closer, sitting at 111,000 or so. Hitting six figures is a truly monumental amount of work, and it's taken Playground over 1,000 hours of work this year alone, across multiple studios, to get through everyone's lines.

According to recent reports, in tandem with this, the team's been making sure you can hear a variety of backgrounds on your journey through the grand adventure. "We were really keen to make sure that there are accents from every corner of the UK, not just your standard fantasy RP accents, but someone from Sheffield, someone from Belfast, someone from Edinburgh," Fulton explains.

"And that brings a certain amount of humor to it naturally," he continues, "because with regional accents, you have funny ways of expressing things, and I think that just adds to the Britishness of the game.".

In a recent development, I'd agree, though I may need subtitles for certain dialects. But that's all part of the charm, really.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Legendary BBC football commentator John "Motty" Motson, who died in 2023 at age 77, is being added to EA Sports FC 27 through "a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself." The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.

Motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames, but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series claims "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "upcoming AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.

Sources indicate that "My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred noted. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole latest set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.".

Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." The BBC report also notes that EA paid the Motson family an undisclosed sum for the right to use John's voice.

According to recent reports, not everyone shares Fred Motson's enthusiasm. While plenty in the EA Sports FC subreddit are excited by the prospect, others refer to it with terms like "shameful," "disrespectful," "gross," and "bloody dark.".

Recent findings suggest that "What a bleak fucking world we live in," redditor forameus2 wrote. "You can't even escape in death.".

"Honestly, it's kind of gross for me," jlo1989 added.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"If anyone from my family uses AI to resurrect me in some perverse way like this, I'll fucking haunt them," niallmul97 wrote.

Peter Caulfield of the Save Our Voices Now campaign against unauthorized voice cloning told the BBC he wouldn't care if Motson had signed a deal with EA allowing it to use his likeness after his death.

"But in life or death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," Caufield mentioned, adding that family members shouldn't "automatically" have the right to grant permission for AI recreations either.

At least one other game studio has taken a very different approach to the subject: Earlier this year, Darkest Dungeon developer Red Hook Studios said it would never use AI to recreate the voice of beloved narrator Wayne June, who died in 2025, despite having explicit permission from June himself to do so.

"I would never, ever erode his incredible and timeless performances by teaching a machine to sound like him," Red Hook co-founder Chris Bourassa stated at the time.

The Japan Actors Union also recently began a push to protect the rights of voice actors with regard to AI, including a proposed ban on using AI to copy a dead actor's voice unless consent had been obtained prior to their death.

Industry News: Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (413 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a newly introduced patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat.
  • In a recent development, the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November.
  • The system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a newly introduced patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat. The patent describes an AI-driven system that listens in on player voice chat following key gameplay moments and later recreates it using in-game characters.

In a recent development, the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November. According to the filing and its diagrams, the system is a self-learning neural network that recognises major gameplay moments - such as kills, longshots, deaths and so on - and records the player's reaction and voice chat from the moment just before and then after they happen. These can be as simple as brief celebratory shouts, groans or yells, or as complex as trash talk.

The system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions. The AI then teaches itself to rapidly identify those when they occur in-game and replicate them.

Although the replicated voice lines don't directly repeat players' own chat, the system does keep a profile of each player it analyses so it can deliver a response tailored to them, including sticking to the same spoken language, which it uses large language models (LLMs) to help identify. The patent describes a filter of sorts to keep NPCs from learning offensive language such as slurs.

According to the patent, the system's reach extends beyond in-game voice chat to also potentially access voice comms from major apps like Discord.

It has been revealed that activision's goal is to create NPCs that can speak naturally, rather than re-use the same pre-recorded lines. The application seems to be limited to multiplayer games, including those with co-op. Think of the generic voice lines spoken by AI-teammates like "cover me" and so on in a PvE game, or the many other similar ones in battle royale and PvP matches that contain dozens or hundreds of players.

Incidentally, the patent talks of replacing those generic messages with learned ones for players who join a match without a microphone, but players can also seemingly allow their in-game avatars to always use generated voices.

As the game industry continues to grapple with the use of generative-AI in game development, Activision's patent seems to be going directly to source, recreating how those LLMs and AI systems got their knowledge to begin with: from humans.

It has been revealed that following the full game list for Awesome Games Done Quick being released a little while ago, GDQ have now published the full schedule for the event running for a week from January 3rd through January 10th in Atlanta (and streamed on Twitch, of course). Included amongst the new games this year are 2026 releases like Queen's Domain, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Ocarina of Time remake, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which all make a lot of sense as games practically made for speedrunning. Belmont's Curse, specifically, is set to be the event's final bonus game, only to be played if donation incentives are met (which I'm sure they will be, it's a Castlevania game at GDQ).

But then, there's also Big Walk, which I'm fascinated by the prospect of trying to speedrun as a group. It's listed as a '12 player showcase', which I can only imagine denotes it as more of a fun experiment to put on a show, rather than a world-record aiming speedrun. The chaos of twelve people trying to work together in Big Walk live on the GDQ stage is a spectacle that has my interest, either way. Also making the cut is train-flipping stunt game Denshattack!, which I simply have to mention got a resounding "✨🚂DENSHATTACK MENTIONED🚂✨" from James in the RPS chat this morning. I can't help but share his excitement, in fairness, since Denshattack! is just that cool.

Recent findings suggest that as for some of the more out-there picks, which I say entirely positively, there's a run of not the DmC reboot, but specifically its bonus Vergil DLC, which is the first time I've heard that mentioned in years. Metroid Prime Origins, a fangame that 'demakes' the famously first-person Metroid Prime into a 2D sidescroller more akin to Zero Mission, is also on the cards; lovely to think there'll be a fresh speedrun for a new Metroid game just a month before Ravenous comes out. And finally, on a personal note because of my own biases, I'm deeply interested to see the Any% run of Yakuza 5 play out; that game is infamous for its ridiculous scope and length, so watching a runner try to get it down to only its most essential parts should be a treat. The schedule estimates around 2 hours for the run, to which I can only say good luck.

We've got some new data coming out about the UK games market in November 2026 today, and unsurprisingly, it's a market that's been absolutely dominated by the launch of GTA 6 last week.

According to the folks at The Game Business, sales of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S rose by a whopping 75% during GTA 6's launch week, which represents the biggest jump for Xbox hardware since 2024.

The PS5 was close behind at 46%, and console sales were up 38% overall (after a 29% increase the week before).

It has been revealed that in terms of UK console sales, PS5 sales rose 46% during the week GTA 6 came out, while Xbox Series S and X sales jumped 75%. It’s the biggest jump for Xbox since 2024. Overall, UK console sales last week were up 38%, which comes on the back of a 29% increase the week prior.

Meanwhile, the controversial "physical" edition of GTA 6 broke numerous records in Europe, serving as the biggest physical launch in Spain's history according to their charts, and selling over 1m physical copies in France in three days.

It was also the biggest physical launch in the UK since FIFA 20 in September 2019, and is the 17th biggest physical launch since records began there in 1995. This is according to data provided by UK data tracker Nielsen IQ.

Industry observers note that "GTA 6 is the biggest physical game launch since 2019, reveals UK data tracker Nielsen IQ. It generated £32 million in revenue in just three days.".

Sources indicate that just last week, on the day of GTA 6's release, we mentioned how Xbox hardware spending in the U.S. was up 42% YoY in October, attributed to the likes of Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6.

It's going to be fascinating to see how the rest of the world stacks up in terms of Xbox sales data from November (which should be revealed over the coming days and weeks), and indeed whether GTA 6's physical edition is also setting records in even more regions. It most likely is - this is a ridiculously popular game after all.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday not only promises sprawling action across the multiverse, but it also features a massive cast (as revealed by that chair promotion last year). However, while the film unites veterans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and stars who predate it, there are some familiar faces who don’t appear to be in the fold. That includes X-Men veterans Halle Berry and Anna Paquin. I’ve been wondering why they weren’t invited back, and Joe and Anthony Russo shared their takes.

Doomsday features several beloved X-Men stars like Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Rebecca Romijn and the late, great Patrick Stewart (in his final film performance). So, for fans like myself, it’s a bit of a head-scratcher that Berry (who played Ororo Munroe/Storm) and Paquin (Marie D'Ancanto/Rogue) apparently weren’t invited to the party. As part of a cover story for this 2026 movie schedule entry, the Russo Brothers were asked about their absences and those of others, with Joe saying this:.

Sources indicate that [The casting] was really targeted. It was really specific.

In fairness, the Russos are shrewd when it comes to assembling (no pun intended) the ensembles for their MCU team-up films. Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame both had specific sets of characters that played into the films’ respective narratives in relevant ways. With that being mentioned, considering the heavy presence of X-Men alums in Doomsday, it’s still somewhat weird that Storm, Rogue, Iceman and more aren’t present when Marsden’s Cyclops notes, “To me, my X-Men.” Still, Anthony Russo added another point:.

Industry observers note that we really do have a process where we see the entire film through each character’s eyes, no matter what the size of their role is. With the X-Men, we got to really deep dive and think about their histories as characters, their experiences, and how this particular moment in time was gonna affect them. There’s such a rich history to them that we really do bring them to the film as if it’s their movie, as well.

Bringing those OGs into the fold seemed to be the realization of a dream not just for the Russos but for producer Kevin Feige as well. Feige’s producing career notably started years ago when Lauren Shuler Donner tapped him as an associate producer on 2000’s X-Men. Now, the super producer is in the position to have his MCU characters interact with the famous mutants for what may be the latter group’s final stand within the multiverse.

According to recent reports, there’s still reason to wonder whether more characters are being kept under wraps ahead of the film’s release. However, earlier this year, when Berry was asked about possibly reprising Storm in Doomsday, she seemed to downplay the idea. The actress does still have plenty of love for the character and the franchise, though, as she celebrated X-Men’s 26th anniversary in July. That post also prompted fans to question her involvement in the upcoming Marvel movie, but nothing has seemingly materialized at this point.

According to recent reports, what is known for sure, though, is that a upcoming team of X-Men will be prominent within the MCU moving forward, as a reboot from director Jake Schreier is on the way. With that, new actors will be taking on the lead roles, with Inde Navarrette and Maya Boyd playing Rogue and Storm, respectively. There’s still time for Marvel to surprise us by having Halle Berry, Anna Paquin and others show up in Doomsday but, if not, there’s always Secret Wars.

Industry observers note that avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18, while Secret Wars is set to follow on December 17, 2027. In the meantime, grab a Disney+ subscription and stream the MCU and X-Men films.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you've been a fan of Grand Theft Auto for a while, you might have noticed a strange absence in GTA 6. While the game is packed full of different activities, the recurring pastime of darts is missing, having been present in GTA 5, GTA Online, and GTA 4.

The reason for the lack of darts in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, according to Rockstar North co-studio lead Rob Nelson, it's a simple case of Rockstar having too little time and resources to make it to a high standard.

Recent findings suggest that nelson told VGC: "The darts one is a contentious one. Even we... You hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to.".

In a recent development, nelson elaborated that since Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar has taken to expanding what were small mini-games into full-on activities. He pointed to basketball in GTA 6 as an example, which you can play in a way that feels like an extension of gameplay with "fluid" movement. Even if it's a relatively small chunk of the game, a lot of time went into making it feel like "a game in its own right", Nelson remarked. And the same is true of pool.

Sources indicate that "A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn't get to," Nelson said. The studio "didn't have the resources" to include it in the game and have it up to par. "It's better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough," he said.

Even without darts, there are plenty of side activities in Grand Theft Auto 6 that help expand Vice City. This includes diving and treasure hunting and fishing, both of which you unlock near the start of the game. If you're looking for a guide of all there is to do in the game, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough is a good place to start. We've also got a breakdown of all the GTA 6 cheats if you needed an extra hand getting through the game.

Industry News: GTA 6 vault: How to open them during significant bank jobs

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1098 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a massive score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.
  • But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.
  • According to recent reports, here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a massive score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.

But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.

According to recent reports, here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.

Sources indicate that your GTA 6 fence, Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun.

Complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, and in Chapter 4 he'll offer you a tip for $10,000. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.

Industry observers note that there are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!

In a recent development, you can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Major Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City International Airport.

Sources indicate that follow the armored car until it parks outside a bank. Watch as one of the drivers gets out and walks into the bank. You can follow him to see where he goes, though bank layouts differ and he may take different routes. He may walk through the front doors, or he may go in a side entrance or a roll-up door in the back.

Once he's all the way inside—not just inside the front doors, but deep into the bank—he'll head to the vault and open it.

In a recent development, you can't open that vault yourself! Only the armored car driver can. That's the trick.

Once the guard is in the back of the bank, begin the robbery. Search for the vault in the back. You may need to use explosives to open the door the guard went through, or you can look for a door you can open with the snap gun. You'll find the vault door open with the armored car driver nearby. Subdue him and grab all the cash off the cart inside the vault.

According to recent reports, there are several safe deposit boxes in the vault you can open for extra loot. Use your focus ability to highlight which boxes you can loot, and shoot them to open them up. You can also blow open all the boxes at once using a grenade or sticky bomb. Grab the loot from each.

Industry observers note that if you really want to clean the place out, there's still all the cash drawers in the front of the bank and a small safe, or multiple safes, somewhere else, usually in an office in the back. You can open these standard safes with safe codes.

Sources indicate that the armored car parked outside has loot in it, too. The thing is, it may despawn while you're inside the bank. If you want to loot it, place a sticky explosive on the rear door, which won't let the truck despawn. (Be stealthy: there's another guard still watching the truck). When you leave the bank after the robbery, detonate the bomb and grab the loot.

The best way to enter a bank is through a back door, if the building has one, (using the snap gun to avoid alarms) or a roll-up door. If the guard you're following goes in the back, he may leave the doors unlocked behind him, and you may not even have to unlock any doors at all to reach the vault. Just be prepared to run into multiple security guards and employees you'll need to subdue.

You will want both Jason and Lucia along for any bank vault jobs you pull. There is so much cash and valuables to grab you'll easily fill up four bags, which requires two people to carry. (You can hand loot bags to your partner by interacting with them and choosing the "Hand over bag" prompt). You'll also want one character to work as crowd control while you're looting the bank.

A silenced gun is a good idea: you want to delay setting off alarms for as long as possible, and if bank employees or citizens hear gunshots they may panic and trigger the alarm, or flee from the bank and call the cops.

In a lot of robberies you can find the security footage and destroy it while the robbery is in progress. Big banks have cloud-based cameras which won't allow you to destroy the footage. Keep a lookout (using focus) for cameras and shoot them out (with silenced pistols) as promptly as you can.

It has been revealed that if an alarm goes off during a vault robbery, you'll get an instant four-star wanted level, which means SWAT trucks, roadblocks, and helicopters. Park your car in a good spot outside so you can jump into it easily, and have some idea of where you want to drive to during your escape.

Breaking: Action RPG Showa American Story seemingly delayed into 2027, with no comment on why from developer NEKCOM

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite being announced back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now.
  • In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.
  • Based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice.

Despite being announced back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now. That seems to have changed, however, as the release date on its Steam page has slipped to 2027 without any sort of announcement as to why.

In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.

Based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice. When I played a demo at Gamescom 2026, I was a little stunned by how awful it felt to play. The protagonist was a blank slate designed to be pretty and nothing more, and the combat was mind-numbingly oversimplified, its challenge mainly derived from the need to wrestle with its janky controls and the noticeable delay between button presses and attacks. In that same interview, Luo notes an awareness of the game being compared to the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series in being a 'wacky' open-world action RPG, saying that he's "happy that players are making that association", as "it means they've recognised Showa American Story as a rich RPG with plenty of content to sink their teeth into." I can respect him taking the comparison in stride, but what I played seemed like a pale imitation of LAD that missed what makes that series more than it seems on the surface.

I can hope that this delay can result in improvements to the critiques the game has faced — Luo did mention that "we've heard many valuable comments regarding the feel of the controls and how the action is presented" — and that Showa American Story releases in a good state sometime in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

This is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it reveals that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The organization’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the upcoming Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

[source famitsu.com, via gematsu.com].

Analyst Suggests Console Prices Won't Drop Until At Least 2028

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too.
  • Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching latest consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.
  • According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too. But if you were hoping 2027 would be the year things finally get cheaper, well, according to S&P boffins, it doesn't look likely.

Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching latest consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.

According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".

"[2028 is] the earliest point at which launching fresh consoles at accessible price points looks prudent,".

In layman's terms, these digits suggest supply might finally begin catching up with demand in 2028, potentially bringing down the cost of PCs and consoles.

DRAM is essentially a console or PC's super-fast short-term memory. Whenever you boot a game, its data is loaded into DRAM so it can be accessed and processed quickly. The more DRAM you have, the bigger and more ambitious games you can play.

The image above gives us a breakdown of the additional DRAM supply expected from each manufacturer, pointing to 2028 as the earliest point at which prices could start to get smaller.

According to recent reports, however, that's relying on a consistent demand from data centres. If it continues to grow, all that additional DRAM could be gobbled up by the AI industry. Likewise, if demand is less popular than predicted, supplies could return quicker.

"If data centre demand grows, then it could swiftly eat into the extra supply...The memory [fabrication facilities] are not expanding with an eye specifically toward the consumer market. They're racking up record revenue and margins on the data centre build-out, so these supply expansions are primarily meant to feed that demand.".

Microsoft's next-gen Xbox Helix console is rumoured to be launching in 2028 with a suspected price tag of over $1,000. Barbour weighed in on Microsoft's Xbox Series supply shortages.

"If Microsoft is suffering from supply shortages with the current Series consoles, as it has said a few times over the past year, then they will almost have to wait for the upstream component supply to shore up before they make a massive push with a newly introduced console.".

According to recent reports, what are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

Metacritic's user review problem worsens, as GTA 6's launch prompts review-bombing for completely unrelated games like Soul Calibur and The Ocarina of Time

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the wake of Grand Theft Auto 6's release and the wave of glowing reviews it received, a war is raging in Metacritic's user reviews, with some of the medium's best games of all time caught in the crossfire.

If you take a look at Metacritics' best games of all time list, you'll see Grand Theft Auto 6 sitting pretty at the top spot. Yet, if you take a gander at some of the others following close behind it, you may notice a sudden increase in very negative reviews from those riding hard for Rockstar's latest release.

Sources indicate that take the user reviews for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which held the top spot for years prior to GTA 6's launch. You can see such pearls of wisdom as: "L Japanese Propaganda. GTA 6 better grafics **** it loser Japanese people," from a user called. Mimm1. Or this gem from danzerthethird: "ass nhbgvfyghjgvfghbjnbhgfycvgjbhguytguyhuytyfgutfgyrc7fytghugytfughtvfygbhjgfycurtyvghbgvfycutryvgcfrgv.".

In a recent development, the same is true for the original Soul Calibur. Its user reviews includes newly delivered pieces of critique like this from user GTABEST2456: "Slop game dethroned by GTA 6, 99 on metacritic N1, now this is third LOOOOOOL, get rekt. I played through and I wish there was less zelda references more niko bellic.".

Even Super Mario Galaxy 2 wasn't safe. Users have taken to review- bombing this game too, an example being BoroqueTsunami who wrote: "Peak Nintendoslop ️ Jump man gimmick. Y'all thought it was sweet until Rockstar pulled up." All of these reviews, across all these non-GTA 6 games, were written following the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

According to recent reports, while it is unclear whether GTA 6 fans shot the first bullet here, or whether anti-GTA 6 Metacritic brigaders are to blame, what is apparent is GTA 6 is itself being hit with a counter-offensive of sorts. "Retaliation for Zelda review bombing," wrote user Lucius26. "I didn't choose this war, but I'll fight it all the same. GTA fans, we were not your enemy. GTA6 just made people mad. You like a bad game, accept that.".

This is all obviously silly and only helps to make the user review section of Metacritic less helpful for people actually trying to get a gist of what these games are like from members of the public. This also stems from a lack of verification on whether people have actually played these games before writing their takes.

Whether events like this will prompt Metacritic to implement some additional quality control remains to be seen, though it has been a continuous problem for a while now and this is hardly the first time review-bombing has been used by some of the more bizarre fans of big-budget releases. In fairness, Metacritic is not the only platform to have suffered from this. Steam, too, has had a history of user review-bombing, with Valve adding features to help curb this over the years.

Recent findings suggest that in the movie about the founding and success of Hershey’s chocolate, Alexandra Daddario plays Milton Hershey’s wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey. They’re beautiful and fitting for the time, and I think it’s so cool that they really helped the actress find her character.

Now, if you’d like to see Alexandra Daddario as Kitty, you can catch Hershey in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A week on from GTA 6's launch, devs at Rockstar Games have officially voted overwhelmingly against a union recognition deal, but those in favor say "we'll keep fighting.".

Sources indicate that that there was a 93.2% turnout in the ballot, which began earlier this month, and of those voters, 1,163 employees voted against the deal, while 381 voted in favor. That's a split of 75.3% to 24.7%.

Sources indicate that rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, says in a statement sent to GamesRadar+ that "we are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6," adding: "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

In a statement shared by Vertical Slice, the IWGB notes that the vote result will "not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights" in the future, "but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives.".

The IWGB Rockstar Games Workers Union also encourages those in favor of the deal not to back down, but to "double down on what we stand for.".

According to recent reports, in a statement sent to GamesRadar+, it indicates: "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for upcoming kinds of conversation to start happening," it continues.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It has been revealed that "People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these fresh discussions can lead us.".

Sources indicate that it says that while "a recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy," it sees this as "one route of many," adding: "At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

"The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.".

A group of Rockstar Games workers began seeking union recognition back in June, with devs hoping for "pay transparency, fairer crunch practices and better flexible working arrangements." This came after Rockstar was accused of union busting late last year following the dismissal of over 30 employees.

This July, Rockstar confirmed it would "arrange to meet" union reps to discuss voluntary recognition – a meeting that the Rockstar union called "a step in the right direction.".

GTA 6 devs are "worried about getting laid off" even after "working on the biggest game of all time.".

Recent findings suggest that dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have announced Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.

Symphony of War II: Dominion Announcement Trailer | Strategy RPG Watch on YouTube.

Dominion's premise mirrors its predecessor in setting a band of heroes from a wide variety of classes, with units ranging from heavy knights and light archers to cannon-lighting artillery and even dragons the size of large dogs; I do have to wonder if an actual hooded horse is one of the units. Over 100 different classes are available, with the core of the game being swapping out these units to create the most effective squads of units for each turn-based battle. As before, it's not just a matter of recruiting soldiers and never thinking about them again until their turn arrives; a cared for army is a strong army (Sun Tzu said that, probably), and nurturing your army with fresh gear, individual perks and specialisation to make the squad work not only on their own, but as a collective.

Sources indicate that phil Hamilton, founder of Dancing Dragon Games, elaborated that "With Symphony of War: Dominion, we’re building on what players loved about the first game while taking the series in a direction we’ve wanted to explore for years. We’re delivering a deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG without sacrificing the feel and flow that made the original special." Symphony of War II: Dominion releases sometime next year, so for now, get thinking about how you'll best take care of your squads. To paraphrase Sun Tzu again, keeping them fed is always a good start.

Publisher Aniplex and developer French-Bread released the main trailer and latest information for fighting game Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina during a TYPE-MOON Times special news program today, revealing the key visual, playable character Satsuki Yumizuka, cross-play, Grand Scenario Mode, the “Act” and “Duel” control modes, and the early purchase bonus.

A Digital Deluxe Edition was also confirmed, which includes the base game and a digital art book.

Industry observers note that in Japan, pre-orders for physical standard and limited editions for PlayStation 5 and Switch will begin on November 26. The latter includes a copy of the game, decorated box featuring artwork by Takashi Takeuchi, an art book, the original soundtrack, an arcade controller button-style tin case featuring artwork by Takeuchi, and a set of three 30-millimeter arcade controller style buttons (Len, White Len, and Satsuki Yumizuka), also by Takeuchi, with a strap.

Upcoming Key Visual by Takashi Takeuchi Revealed!

Industry observers note that aniplex unveiled a newly drawn illustration by Takashi Takeuchi, who is handling the character designs for this title. In addition to the two characters, Shiki Tohno and Arcueid, the visual features Ren, White Ren, and Satsuki Yumizuka, who will make their debut as playable characters in the upcoming game.

Satsuki Yumizuka Makes Her Debut as a Fresh Playable Character.

The new trailer not only introduces the new character, and new game play systems added specifically in this title, but also the Grand Scenario Mode created by Kinoko Nasu.

Industry observers note that the video also features the game’s theme song, Welcome To My Dream (feat. 310), produced by Spiral Ladder.

New Battle System and Cross-Platform Multiplayer.

Sources indicate that during the most recent stream of TYPE-MOON Times: Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina Latest Information Special, Ryosuke Kanemoto as Shiki Tohno and Yohei Azagami as Mikhail Roa Baldamyon were joined by development director Kamo Serizawa. Together they revealed the latest information on the game, including newly introduced game systems added in this title, which includes the series’ first cross-platform versus mode, as well as the Grand Scenario Mode created by Kinoko Nasu. The versus play also features the new playable characters Ren and White Ren.

First Cross-Platform Multiplayer Feature.

This title in the Melty Blood series is slated to be the first of its kind in supporting cross-platform play, which allows players to battle against more players across different platforms.

According to recent reports, the Act control scheme, which allows players to move the character with simple controls by activating special moves with the press of a single button. This is recommended for those upcoming to fighting games or the Melty Blood series.

Recent findings suggest that the Duel control scheme, which lets players enjoy more authentic battles by utilizing precise controls through traditional command inputs. This play style is recommended for those familiar with fighting games or players who want to delve deeper into the game mechanics.

Grand Scenario Mode includes new story by Kinoko Nasu.

The new Grand Scenario Mode is a large-scale scenario feature newly added to this title.

According to recent reports, players can enjoy a story written exclusively for this game by Kinoko Nasu that focuses on the protagonist, Shiki Tohno. The story is presented through a variety of narrative techniques, and more information is available on the official website, as well as during the TYPE-MOON Times: Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina Latest Information Special.

Round call voices for Ren, White Ren, and Satsuki Yumizuka will be added to the main game.

Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina is due out for PlayStation 5, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC via Steam on April 22, 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency.

Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings.

On whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche noted during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question.".

Blanche also noted that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal.

"A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer said on Tuesday.

In a recent development, according to sources speaking to Reuters, Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, the latter of which is the firm associated with Alice Huang (no relation), the woman with whom Huang admitted to having an affair. (The CEO also reportedly had affairs with Nvidia employees.).

In his return address to Nvidia staff, Huang said (via Marisa Kabas) that the tech giant's board opted to bring him back of their own accord, not because of pressure from the Trump administration. That statement is contradicted by Trump himself, who told CNBC that he "convinced" the Nvidia board to bring Huang back.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Nvidia's share price shot up following Huang's reinstatement, but dropped again by several points on Wednesday, and remains about 21.5% lower than it was at the start of this year. Trump is an Nvidia investor, and Nvidia donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom project.

Huang is scheduled to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

Tech Report: GTA 6 can run at 60fps on Xbox Series X if you use a glitch, but there's a catch

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (393 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro.
  • It has been revealed that reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X.
  • Industry observers note that in a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro. The game doesn't offer a 60fps performance mode or an option to unlock the frame-rate, but one industrious player has managed to do it anyway on Xbox.

It has been revealed that reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game.

Industry observers note that in a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates.

Sources indicate that first, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz.

Before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume.

It has been revealed that after the second game launches, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user said the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments.

Unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this glitch, so they run at their normal speed.

As much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are declared and Xbox doesn't make a major deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

Sources indicate that in other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and new Fallout games where it felt like they were announced without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is declared / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

Let's see what happens in the New Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

"Game feel is impossible to copy": CEO of Probably Stolen publisher tinyBuild says devs "shouldn't be afraid" of AI clones

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that genAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI.
  • Nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being important in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually.
  • He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed.

Recent findings suggest that genAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it.".

Nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being important in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually. And that seems to be changing fundamentally." He adds that maintaining a short gap also helps as, to put it simply, "people have short memories, right?" And, unfortunately, he's right; there are so many games coming out that adding something to your wishlist often feels like resigning it to remembering it exists six months later.

He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed. But then, he clarifies that the reason it seemed so easy was a lack of care. "There's a reason that every kind of AI slop game feels the same; it's because when you try to make something from zero, AI will multiply your skills, and zero times a thousand is still zero." The people claiming to 'develop' recomps do not care for making a game that feels right, or even one that works; they care only for the short-lived dopamine of being popular on Twitter for fifteen minutes before another slop copy rears its head (and is inevitably revealed to be jankware). Nichiporchik specifies that "game feel is impossible to copy; as long as you have a great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be okay." 'Game feel' is one of the vaguest terms that exists in this field, but I do feel that it refers to something tangible and immediately noticeable when it's gone.

Sources indicate that for example, I've recently been replaying the wonderful Celeste, and the 'game feel' of its wavedashing is core to making the practice of blazing through levels so engaging. The wavedash works the same every time, due to precise programming from Extremely OK Games spending time and effort painstakingly ensuring it did in the interest of consistency and unity in movement mechanics. You can't make good art without caring about the quality, even if there are now faster ways to knock together a 'working' game. To borrow an overused but still salient phrase: AI could never.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gaming tech giant Nvidia has decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, despite allegedly saying it wouldn't, and despite a string of extramarital affairs and investigations into alleged bullying, workplace harassment, and humiliation.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's Chair Harvey C. Jones announced on behalf of the Nvidia's board today - the same person reported as saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Firm. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's chief financial officer.".

In the same press release, Huang stated he was "honoured" to return to the organization "at the beginning of a new industrial revolution". "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said.

Sources indicate that however, the investigation into one of Huang's extramarital affairs - the one with the person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy - will "proceed to conclusion". The manufacturer also said it formed a "National Security and Export Control Committee", with independent directors, in relation to this.

Recent findings suggest that huang resigned on 12th November a few days after his affair with the alleged Chinese spy came to light. Two subsequent affairs - both said to be with Nvidia employees and therefore his subordinates - were unearthed not long after, putting increased pressure on Huang and Nvidia.

Since his departure, Nvidia stock has tanked, and as news of his reinstatement spreads around the world, it has sharply recovered again.
