💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar hired a former Gran Turismo pro to help master the car handling in GTA 6.
  • Lewis Bentley, a 2018 GT World Series Finalist, indicates he spent the last three-and-a-half years with the studio’s physics team, working on how the cars feel to drive.
  • Recent findings suggest that in a now-deleted YouTube video – watched by GT Planet – he notes he helped “put the auto in Grand Theft Auto”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar hired a former Gran Turismo pro to help master the car handling in GTA 6.

Lewis Bentley, a 2018 GT World Series Finalist, indicates he spent the last three-and-a-half years with the studio’s physics team, working on how the cars feel to drive.

Recent findings suggest that in a now-deleted YouTube video – watched by GT Planet – he notes he helped “put the auto in Grand Theft Auto”. He’s credited as a developer on the Physics Development Group, and he said in his video that the entire team was “amazing”.

It has been revealed that the Edinburgh-based dev is no stranger to real-life racing, as it fielded its own winning team in the 24 Hours of Nürburgring event four years ago. Ben Lyons, who made up part of the squad, was the Technical Director in charge of physics on the title.

I personally really love the way cars feel in the game.

Each type has its own distinctive handling model, and you can really feel the difference when you go to a Mod Shop and tune your car to taste.

It doesn’t have the distinctive heavy handling of GTA 4, but it’s also not quite as arcadey as GTA 5 either – I’d say it sits somewhere comfortably between the two, which is a good place to be.

I love all the extra work that’s been put into the DualSense’s haptic feedback, too; the way you can physically feel the change of grip between the different road surfaces – it’s impressive stuff.

Industry observers note that I just wish Rockstar had put a little more energy into the races themselves, because they do rely on aggressive rubber banding, which is pretty frustrating. Considering how meticulously the rest of the game is crafted, it would have been nice if a bit more thought went into this aspect.

All in all, though, I’m not surprised to learn GTA 6 had real-life race car drivers and pro Gran Turismo players on its team. You spend a good chunk of your time in Leonida driving, and I think by and large Rockstar really nailed this important aspect of the game.

That last point's a bit of contention in the community, given hunters are out-performing other classes in damage, but given we're just three weeks into the game with a couple of weeks left to go before the raid tier, I'm not sweating the lack of an immediate nerf bat.

Sources indicate that right, there's my journalistic obligation taken care of. Here's why I'm (not) upset.

Scarlet Subterfuge—and In Dreams—is widely considered one of the crappiest quests in Classic, and given this is a game that's already rife with inconvenience—inconvenience I am usually all for—that's saying something. In it, you need to go and find Highlord Taelan Fordring, son of Tirion Fordring, and remove the scarlet-coloured wool from his eyes.

Story-wise, this quest kicks ass. You're finding the son of the guy who wielded the Ashbringer. Realising his life has been a lie, he hulks out, cleaving down his former scarlet allies, and marches out of the fortress side-by-side with you. Mechanically, it sucks so much, dude.

To reach Fordring the younger, you need to go halfway across the zone, talk to an illusionist hermit, and don a disguise. Then you need to jog all the way up to where Taelan is to give him the news.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The only downside is that this disguise lasts for 30 minutes, and escorting Taelan, at least with the current strategy (more on this later) lasts for about 20 minutes. And if you don't have the disguise on, he's hostile to you, even if you're just restarting the escort quest. So that means that if anybody else is doing the quest by the time you get there, you need to either:.

The actual escort is annoying, too: Since Taelan can technically handle the Scarlet Crusade on his lonesome, accepted practice for this quest has been to simply let him handle things. Which both makes it take ages and makes it difficult to find a group so that you can do it the intended way.

Recent findings suggest that as a cherry on top, you can't really skip this quest outright as it gives some really powerful pre-BiS endgame items. Still, I persevered, I did it yesterday, and Blizzard, uh. Blizzard gave the disguise an hour-long duration literally today.

"Western Plaguelands - The Scarlet Illusion granted during the quest 'Scarlet Subterfuge' now lasts an hour (was 30 minutes).".

This doesn't make the quest any less of a headache to finish, but hey—at least if someone else is already doing it, you won't have to jog back to your hag friend or play the log-in, log-out Hokey Pokey until he respawns. Good for you.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

Recent findings suggest that for one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY.

Industry observers note that one especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come quickly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3.

Sources indicate that as you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

Industry observers note that this GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr.

It has been revealed that here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

It has been revealed that if you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

Christmas in July? Why Stop There?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays?
  • Industry observers note that consider it!
  • According to recent reports, if the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Industry observers note that consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a Latest Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

According to recent reports, if the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

In a recent development, so we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in Upcoming York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

Sources indicate that but why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Industry observers note that let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in Latest York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a massive turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that one of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-important executable file, which was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek.

Recent findings suggest that as documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools. Going by Hendricks's posts, which are based on watching a Leonida stream, much of the recomp's creation seems to have consisted of one or more high school kids typing prompts like "work faster", while spending hundreds or thousands of dollars in usage fees.

The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds.

As reported by PCG, the Leonida Discord server has now been shut down, and the Github repository for the recompilation's code has been nuked. Hendricks has shared an alleged takedown request from a representative of Take-Two Interactive, according to which Github have taken action against 3,007 forks (that is, duplicates for the purposes of making a separate version) from the original Leonida repo. Meanwhile, somebody has set up a leaderboard to chart the progress of several other GTA 6 recomp projects. I'm sure Take-Two's IP enforcement teams appreciate their efforts.

A few days prior to GTA 6's release on console last week, Rockstar North's former tech director Obbe Vermeij told RPS that the GTA makers would release the PC version sooner than anticipated to avoid losing any cash to generative AI rip-offs. IGN subsequently asked Take-Two's CEO Strauss Zelnick for his thoughts on this. Zelnick replied that the tech giant are "not in the least cavalier" about the risk, but are confident people would rather play the game as Rockstar intended.

Although GTA 6 continues to smash records as the highest-rated game of all time, it hasn't been without any bugs to speak of – some of which are proving so persistent, Rockstar's own patches aren't wiping them out of the new Grand Theft Auto game.

Sources indicate that one especially notorious bug – a bug that Rockstar's first GTA 6 patch didn't manage to tackle despite promising to – sees players' in-game weather locked. If you didn't already know it, the weather is supposed to be dynamic (realistic, even), changing over time from sunny to rainy to stormy to… you get it. Unfortunately, though, it's not properly swapping for many fans, resulting in a far more stagnant experience and reduced immersion. And while the recent GTA 6 patch apparently didn't fix the bug for affected players, fans on Twitter have come to the rescue. "I found a working fix for the weather bug in GTA 6," one writes. "You just have to clear your PS5's cache. It's super easy and takes like two minutes." They then outline how to do so, from shutting down their PlayStation 5 to clearing the system cache in safe mode.

I found a working fix for the weather bug in GTA 6. LETS GOOOO. You just have to clear your PS5’s cache. It’s super easy and takes like two minutes. > Turn off your PS5 completely. > Press and hold the power button until it beeps to enter safe mode. > Go to option 6 and select clear system cache. > Your system will restart and then the weather not changing glitch will be fixed. I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather. I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted, thank you so much to @mauricioce85796 for leaving a reply advising me to do this. Unreal that this wasn’t patched before release but thankfully it is indeed solvable.November 26, 2026.

Sources indicate that "Your system will restart and then the weather not changing glitch will be fixed," they state, going on to say it took them quite some time to figure the fix out. "I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven't experienced any dramatic weather. I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm." The poster credits a fellow fan for the fix, concluding that it's "unreal that this wasn't patched before release but thankfully it is indeed solvable.".

Comments see other players thanking the two for the fix and confirming that it does indeed work. "Can confirm," reads on. "Weather is more varied!" Another adds, "It worked for me too! I'd never seen storm clouds forming like that in my 50 hours of gameplay!" Hopefully, however, Rockstar rolls out another official fix soon, and fans don't feel the need to crack into their PS5's deeper settings to get weather working.

Netflix's The Body was one of the unexpected hits of the 2026 TV schedule. While it's still yet to be confirmed whether we'll get to stream a second season with a Netflix subscription, it feels like the odds are looking good. So I'm glad the executive producers/showrunners are already shooting down some fan theories before any new episodes come out.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, creator Quinn Shephard and co-showrunner Gina Gammell didn't tell Glamour all the biggest secrets surrounding Grace and whether this is truly spiritual or classic Catholic School drama, Luckily, though, fans did learn a couple of key details. I'm happy about both of these theories being addressed, especially the one that sounds like good news for Leo.

It has been revealed that if you're a fan of Leo and think he's too pure for this world, Quinn Shepard confirming he did not bring a snake to the Halloween party should bring you some comfort. It's been theorized that Leo brought his pet snake to the party, perhaps in an attempt to heal Grace. This was supported by the fact that Leo and Grace came from a cult called Signs Following, which used snake handling as a means of showing the faith of its followers.

According to recent reports, additionally, Leo seemed concerned about other characters outside of his family seeing the snake during the investigation into Grace's coma. With this context, it's possible that Leo was just concerned about hiding their true religious beliefs, as they lied about being Catholics to get rehomed after leaving West Virginia.

I'm so glad the EPs have also confirmed the Lions won't be going to jail after what happened to Grace. I thought that was a possibility, given Anya's confession and the various details about the party that came out toward the end of Season 1.

I Just Watched The Trailer For Netflix's JonBenèt Ramsey Drama, And I Feel A Bit Uneasy.

Industry observers note that while I'm all for accountability in teen dramas, especially when it comes to Riverdale's Archie Andrews, I'll let it slide for The Body. Sending Anya or any of the Lions to jail or prison for their actions at the party would've created a major genre shift in the story, and I'm far more interested in the story remaining around the school after Season 1's ending.

In a recent development, of course, we still have to wait for official word on Season 2 of The Body. While I think Netflix should be bullish on a renewal given the talented young cast and the fact it's been on Netflix's Top 10 charts in recent weeks, there's really no telling what the streamer will decide to do with the series. It's a well known fact that the manufacturer has canceled plenty of shows way too soon, so we best just cross our fingers and hope a Grace-sized miracle grants the series a renewal soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year.
  • "This fresh system isn't really new," Newman wrote.
  • According to recent reports, similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year. That rough start has it in need of a redemption arc, which the Rust devs are hoping will be powered by going free-to-play and making changes like the revamp of sandbox mode they've just rolled out.

"This fresh system isn't really new," Newman wrote. "It's the exact same system that Garry's Mod uses. I hold my hands up here, I thought that spawning from the cloud was better...but I was wrong. There definitely is something a lot nicer about installing a big model pack and then having everything right there. I'm sorry it took me so long to come around to realising this.".

According to recent reports, similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well". "I'm excited by all the possibilities of it," he continued. "Obviously there aren't a ton of addons right now but what we do have is showing a LOT of potential, and that's only going to grow. I've been going through improving things that feel outdated or stupid. I'm resisting bending it all too far, I want it to stay kind of familiar for everyone, but I think we can improve a few things in our newly introduced engine.".

Sources indicate that A number of old school sandbox props, such as chunks of robotics, wheels, gears, and hunks of steel girder are on their way back, while Facepunch are finally ready to add in water. "It has waves," Newman wrote of the latter. "The physics objects get tossed around in the waves. You can go underwater, and swim, and there's caustics and fog and particles and post process effects and stuff." Also, NPCs now "live directly in the engine" making it easier to set up a fight club.

A simplified menu and a whole bunch of performance and dev-focused tweaks round out this update, so go through the full notes if you're keen to read about the likes of workshop mounts and VRAM fragmentation.

As of writing, S&box is still yet to go free-to-play, a change Newman and co previously remarked is coming "towards the end of the year". If it can nail recapturing the classic GMod magic with updates that players actually want, I think it stands a chance of a comeback. However, as its lifespan thus far has proven, it's harder to rely on high quality user-made games within a game than ever before in an age when people can just resort to using generative AI for an ever-increasing number of things.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a latest report, the manufacturer is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

Sources indicate that the information comes from a upcoming report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the organization is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of shows based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

According to recent reports, indeed, many more video game-based reveals are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

Sources indicate that but none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

In Xenoblade Chronicles 3 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, you will join Noah and Mio, members of the opposing nations of Keves and Agnus, as they embark on a stirring journey through a war-torn world that harbors a dark secret. Master real-time RPG combat and enjoy newly voiced event scenes, enhanced 4K resolution in TV mode (with compatible television), full HD in handheld mode, and smoother, sharper gameplay at 60 frames per second.

Pairs of characters can also Interlink to form a mighty Ouroboros capable of taking down the most threatening enemies with powerful Arts.

You can also test your strength against waves of enemies in the fresh Heroes’ Vault mode. Here, with each enemy you defeat, you’ll power up a gauge you can use to enhance your abilities and gain additional allies. But choose wisely—you’ll need to prepare well to defeat the almighty foe awaiting you at the end of each mission!

  • In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise. Diplomacy! The soul of any Total War game. They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "upcoming heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day.

Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.

In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".

As regards "believable agendas", Creative Assemble want the campaign AI to display both a survival instinct and the ability to "pursue its own interests instead of primarily being an antagonist to the player". These agendas will span the game's Politics, Economy, and Families systems, with dynastic considerations affecting behaviour. They want you to be able to read another ruler's intent by tracking back through their past actions. They want weaker factions to sue for peace or seek sensible alliances, rather than "stubbornly being entrenched in a war it is bound to lose". Aww, but I love it when Scotland does that.

The game will aim for a balance of long-term thinking and opportunism, with AI leaders pouncing on short-term prospects even as they keep the whole in mind. And then there are inconvenient "ripple effects": you might get involved with a neighbouring succession crisis because you don't want to deal with the fallout if, you know, That Guy takes the throne.

Speaking of borders, Creative Assembly also want would-be treaty-makers to think harder about terrain and transportation. "For example: You finally reach a faraway realm with your diplomat, opening diplomatic relations to a realm far beyond your initial sphere of influence," Wojs goes on. "Relations are positive, but meaningless due to the lack of physical proximity. Once that faraway realm has access to a port, a trade route can finally be established. This leads to an exchange in culture and trade, and may finally allow you to recruit foreign units into your service.".

Sources indicate that I have to say, I do find a lot of this language either broadly familiar from previous Twars, or too general to reveal much. There is, however, a closing in-game anecdote from principal designer Thomas Schut that digs into the detail. Schut gives the example of you sending a diplomat to negotiate a 10 year non-aggression pact greased by recognition of another ruler's royal title, in return for their vassalage. Sending a diplomat allows you to negotiate on the spot, but if you'd rather not spare a diplomat, you can also dispatch sealed letters at the price of not being able to see and respond immediately to the other faction's reaction.

Rulers can make public claims to cities, calling on other rulers to support them. Simply conquering and annexing them will damage your standing in every court. You can also forge claims to cities, if only as insurance against wanting to own them someday. Get enough rulers to back you, and you'll be able to throw around grander pronouncements about what you're divinely entitled to. You are the Emperor of Everything! Coalitions will apparently form and fragment over years, old friends turning on each other as their dark plots come to light.

Sources indicate that the joy of Cao Cao puppetry notwithstanding, I don't play Total War for the chance to thrash out cunning pacts with bots. I am here to put my archers behind my spearfolk - and hope the other side's cavalry don't notice the cutthroats I've stationed in the woods. I'm more interested in what I've read about Medieval 3's regional levies system. Still, it does sound like Creative Assembly are serious about giving you things to do besides putting other wannabe kings to the sword.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since.
  • Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era.
  • That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” says Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”.

Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” notes Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”.

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” states Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”.

It certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”.

Bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

In a recent development, dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

It has been revealed that for actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” says Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”.

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

Industry observers note that “I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” states Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”.

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”.

In a recent development, and that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers.
  • According to recent reports, the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

In a recent development, after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

According to recent reports, the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

"I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

Sources indicate that "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've mentioned before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Recent findings suggest that before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but quickly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

Incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

It has been revealed that rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not announced GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.

A modder using AI to create The Last of Us Part 2 multiplayer that Naughty Dog never gave us notes Sony can't do much even if it wanted to shut it down.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, Sony put the brakes on one such mod. YouTuber Speclizer unveiled their mod at the start of this year, but two months ago, they announced it was canceled after they received a cease and desist from Sony Interactive Entertainment. However, another has emerged in the form of Twelve Weeks (via IGN), with the developer releasing a mod earlier this week featuring 4v4 team battles.

The creator, Kellie, admitted on Twitter that AI was used in its development, saying, "Claude code was used for most of the project." However, they note that no AI artwork has been used, with the dev explaining she made the artwork herself.

Over on a YouTube video for the mod, the developer's account claims that Speclizer's mod was subject to a cease and desist because it was paywalled, but "mine is released already for free and in open source." However, even if the devs do receive a letter from Sony, it's claimed that "since people have the source code to the full mod already, there ain't much they can do even if they do shut me down.".

Industry observers note that naughty Dog was creating The Last of Us Online based on the second game for some time before it was canceled in 2023. Word out of the studio was very favorable, with its director, Vinit Agarwal, saying some who worked on it thought it was "the best multiplayer game they've ever played.".

The Last of Us had a shockingly great multiplayer mode, strong enough to rival other substantial hitters of the Xbox 360 and PS3 generation. Who knows how the sequel's would've been, but with how much better the gameplay was in The Last of Us Part 2 was, I reckon it could've been great.

"We're not done with The Last of Us": Neil Druckmann confirms Naughty Dog has "a couple projects in the works," even if the TV show is ending.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Capcom announced as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT.
  • In a recent development, the publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with plans to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date. Its online services will cease as of late September 2027, rendering it unplayable, with the game set to be delisted from stores in March.

Capcom announced as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement," they wrote.

In a recent development, the publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with plans to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027. Those who already own Exoprimal will be able to re-download it in the time between it being pulled from stores and the server shutdown in September, meaning there's plenty of time to hop in for a final few rounds of dino shooting if you fancy.

It's long seemed like only a matter of time before the dino shooter was taken offline, with Capcom having stopped releasing fresh seasonal additions to it all the way back in July 2024. So, this seems more like a natiral petering out than an instance of an online game being cut down in its prime or not long after launch, as we've seen recently with extreme cases like Highguard. As such, one would hope there's a chance plenty of Exoprimal devs have already been redirected onto other Capcom games, minimising the amount who might be left in the often precarious position of having nothing immediate to work on following this shutdown.

Sources indicate that it's fair to say Ed Thorn (RPS in peace) wasn't a fan of Exoprimal on reviewing it at launch. "I thought Exoprimal somehow managed to make dinosaurs versus mechs, aka the coolest concept ever, boring in my review-in-progress,"he wrote. "I held out hope it would improve, though, as lots of commenters assured me it's fun side would finally surface. "Just play several more hours and things really open up! Variety in the dinos, in the modes, in just about everything!". To some extent, they were right. There are fun moments to be had as you queue up for Dino Survival and suddenly, remarkably, things have changed a bit.

"But the game doesn't respect your time. It forces you to sit through hours of repetitive dino-slaying and then only offers you the chance, the chance to slay dinos in a way that isn't excruciatingly samey. Even as someone who finds the fun in mindless carnage, I'd much rather ditch my mech suit and let the dinosaurs run rampant. The dinosaurs don't deserve this.".

That's not exactly as positive a eulogy as the one offered by Capcom, but not all games are destined to stick the landing and be universally beloved mega-hits, especially those wading into the live service maelstrom.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, to say that Paper Tiger had me stressed would be an understatement.
  • It has been revealed that it was looking like there really wouldn't be any way out of the danger Irwin (Miles Teller), his brother Gary (Adam Driver) and his family were in.
  • After seeing his brother one last time at Scott's birthday party, Gary lies and claims he's leaving the country, assuring Irwin things are going to be ok and gifting him his car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, to say that Paper Tiger had me stressed would be an understatement. James Gray's crime drama, which just arrived on the 2026 movie schedule, had me on the edge of my seat throughout, and then reeling from those final scenes. I want to get into what happened at the end of the movie, and what the writer/director told us about it. I can't do that without 🛑 MAJOR spoilers from the Adam Driver movie - if you haven't seen Paper Tiger and have somehow wandered into this article, now's your chance to leave! Be sure to catch it in theaters or wait until it's available on streaming.

It has been revealed that it was looking like there really wouldn't be any way out of the danger Irwin (Miles Teller), his brother Gary (Adam Driver) and his family were in. Gary, as it turned out, wasn't the kind of cop who would cross major ethical lines by working with the Russian mob - at least not for any kind of job that isn't above board. When money wasn't going to be enough to satisfy Simeon Bogoyavich (Victor Ptak), and Gary wasn't willing to work with him, the only way to make things right was for Gary to accept the terms of Simeon's deal: his life in exchange for his brother's (and his family's) safety. That was Simeon's price, and Gary agreed to pay it.

After seeing his brother one last time at Scott's birthday party, Gary lies and claims he's leaving the country, assuring Irwin things are going to be ok and gifting him his car. We see him get emotional when he's by himself in his rental car, which I interpret as him accepting his fate, as terrible as it is.

Later, he drives toward the airport and waits until he sees the Russian guys tailing him. He mutters something about wanting to take them out with him, and then pulls off to the side of the road, where he hides in a nearby field. The guys creep around among the stalks and Gary shoots a couple of them, the gunshot sounds muffled by the planes overhead. He's inevitably shot by one of them and dies.

Industry observers note that at Irwin's house, his wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) has snuck off to have surgery on her brain tumor. She's last seen blowing a kiss to her husband and kids, who are still asleep. Later that morning, Scott is helping Ben study, and Irwin listens to a message about job opportunities now that his and his brother's consulting business is registered. The tone is uplifting in the Pearl house, despite what we know. Does this mean that everything is going to be ok, and the Russian mob boss will keep his end of the deal now that Gary is dead?

As writer/director James Gray told us, he has hope that things will be ok for the family.

In a recent development, I think they're going to be all right. Somehow I have hope. You get he gets a message that this the better business or the business bureau or whatever it is, is going to has all this great jobs lined up for him and his children are studying for school very dutifully.

According to recent reports, in the final scene within the Pearl house, they don't yet know about Hester's situation, though it seems unlikely that she'll keep that a secret for long. This family may be out of the woods with this Russian mob situation, but that doesn't mean everything will be perfect in the coming weeks and months. As Gray put it:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, I mean, he's got something terrible coming with his wife that he doesn't know about, right? But that's life. You know, bad things and good things happen in equal measure. We almost have to kind of accept that that's what our fates are as human beings. But I think he'll be all right.

It has been revealed that the more I think about Paper Tiger's ending, the more this makes sense to me and adds to my overall satisfaction to this suspenseful and emotional film. Hester's tumor is nobody's doing, just the tragic nature of life, unfair though it may be. So much of what transpired in the film had to do with choices and actions, but in the case of Hester, it's just the cards she was dealt, and she and her family will have to face that.

Sources indicate that I did personally feel a note of hope in that final scene. Because Irwin and his sons weren't aware of what happened to Gary, or what was going in with Hester, they were just going about their morning routines. It felt like we were seeing a glimpse of what everyday life would look like for these three Pearl men, and it was simple and safe. It's the calm before another storm, but there's a note of optimism that they'll get through it and have each other for support.

Kelly put her life-long love of movies, TV and books to greater use when she joined CinemaBlend as a freelance TV news writer in 2006, and went on to serve as the site’s TV Editor before joining the staff full-time in 2011 and moving over to other roles at the site. At present, she’s an Assistant Managing Editor who spends much of her time brainstorming and editing features, analyzing site data, working with writers and editors on content planning and the workflow, and obsessing over the best movies and TV highlights. She graduated from SUNY Cortland with BA in Communication Studies and a minor in Cinema Studies. When she isn't working, she's probably thinking about work, or reading (or listening to a book), and making sure her cats are living their absolute best feline lives.

#212134. Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1946 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1946 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that at first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know.
  • Luke’s knowledge is beautiful but the students also find him approachable.
  • The bleeps and blips start from the machines as the students start playing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.

Luke’s knowledge is beautiful but the students also find him approachable. As Jason shares: "It’s really inspirational for kids coming onto a bus that they can talk to someone younger like Luke, who knows his stuff and has made something incredible happen." One student asks where Minecraft is and Luke explains that it doesn’t fit the parameter of being more than twenty years old yet, sharing details of when it was published and by who. Roblox could be included, but Luke isn’t keen because of recent controversies around safety. When this group are reluctantly herded off the bus by even more reluctant teachers, another heads in with just a little gap for resetting the machines and cramming a biscuit.

The bleeps and blips start from the machines as the students start playing. One teacher stops at the Atari 2600 and shares that her family has just bought her one. She is loving the daily dose of nostalgia. Luke and Jason move up and down the bus answering questions, resetting machines and showing the students their collection of old phones. One student winces at he is passed the bag that would have carried the battery for a Panasonic EB-3600 "brick" phone from 1989. When Jason says his dad had one, they give that look of pity reserved for anyone over 30 but are also incredulous that anyone would lug that around, especially when the phone could only do calls. When Jason asks if anyone would like to break an iPhone and have a look inside, all of the hands shoot up. He then talks about memory, RAM and chips, brings out a floppy disk; and tells the tale of where the expression "computer bug" came from. Still, it's the game on a tape - Jungle Story for the Commodore 64 - which they all turn away from screens to see. Perhaps we have Stranger Things to thank, but the tape has retro currency and they all think it’s sick.

It has been revealed that the event is being run by East Sussex Careers Hub and is specifically aimed at students with SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities). More than twenty-five schools turn up and most teachers leave with a flyer, chatting to colleagues about where the bus could park onsite. Jason claims that the response to the bus, since Retro Reset's launch as a registered charity in August 2025, has been phenomenal, and they could easily fill a full week with visits. For now, he is juggling it with work commitments.

The bus was Luke’s idea and inspired by a visit to The Centre for Computing History in Cambridge, where visitors can get their hands on home computers and consoles from decades gone by. The family started thinking about what was possible and finally, after Luke finished college, began kitting out the bus: buying or accepting donations of hardware, researching which monitors would work with the ancient systems, and installing it all within the cabin.

On a basic level, the charity is telling the story of how technology has iterated. But by allowing visitors to take apart their machines, and giving brief lessons in coding with Basic, it also pulls the veil back on the work that goes into making a game - while opening students' eyes to what they could create themselves. "I guess it’s bridging the gap between the polished and finished latest game," Jason claims, "which could be perceived as not achievable for them, to seeing how all that coding came about. Other than making sure they are really accurate with their typing; they realise that coding can be quite simple and something that they can actually do. I would go further and say that when they have written some code, nearly all of them have a major smile on their face." This, he hopes, might be the spark for some students to get into coding, especially for PC games, where under-18s are an underrepresented demographic.

It also hit the road as the popularity of retro gaming continued to surge. According to a Consumer Reports survey published last February, 14% of US gamers regularly play games made before 2000. This is reflected in the staggering stat that the retro gaming market is estimated to be worth $3.8 billion globally, with a projected rise to $8 billion by 2033. Retro-focused videos on YouTube and TikTok rack up millions of views of views, and communities formed on reddit or Discord - some with hundreds of thousands of members - discuss nothing else.

Nostalgia is playing a huge part. Atari’s Implicit Conversations is built on just this, creating retro games for modern consoles like PlayStation 5 or the Nintendo Switch. For Luke, though, this misses the point. He likes the click when you put a cartridge in a machine; and he likes that he is just him and the game. The parents of visiting students appreciate this too, and often share how overwhelming it feels to keep their kids safe in the online gaming environment. "Parents of younger children [tell us that] they hate that Minecraft and Roblox can allow their kids to play against perceived strangers. Even the more technical parents say they still miss safety measures and would prefer the games not be online at all," Jason explains.

According to recent reports, last month, Ofcom published its Growing Up Gaming summary report, which found that almost two-thirds (64%) of parents of three to 17 year olds who game online are concerned about their child talking to strangers through games or their chat functions. And, while the vast majority of young players go online without incident, it is true that those who use chat functions will likely interact with strangers. The same research found that more than half (55%) of children who game online say they play with people they have never met offline at least sometimes, while one in five (20%) do so all or most of the time they play.

According to recent reports, by contrast, Jason claims that not one student has asked if they can get online, and he’s also never seen one get out their phone when they’re on the bus. Perhaps it is a welcomed break. "We offer a completely safe environment to come and experience these games and machines. That's really what we're here for," he states.

In a recent development, luke shares too that he became nervous of the data he was sharing with gaming companies, and conscious that this was all being stored, thus making it vulnerable to breaches. He also baulked at what he felt was a constant money grab from gaming companies, including moves that render games unsupported or completely obsolete. Retro gaming is cheap in comparison and therefore more accessible, especially for younger players. "When you tell them that they can get an old console for less than £100 and often games come free when you buy them second hand, their ears really prick up," Jason says. "For a lot of the youngsters, the cost of modern gaming equipment is unattainable. And of course, we explain that they could take old computers and laptops and then load free operating software onto them. This gets them online, often for free. Once they are there, they can game.".

John W. Champeau is founder of Champ Games, a Connecticut-based venture, which develops retro games system primarily for the Atari 2600. He has Scramble, Galagon, Gorf Arcade and Elevator Agent on his line-up. He agrees that price point is a huge part of the appeal of retro gaming. "Atari has released a line of "+" systems that are modern reinterpretations of the class Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware, but at a lower price point but with modern conveniences such as HDMI support, firmware updates, and new controllers," he notes. These systems can also play older cartridges that were released back in the day. "This means that the games themselves can be acquired at a low cost as well, sometimes even free if someone is lucky enough to know someone with a box of old Atari carts in their basement or attic.".

But there may also be something intrinsically different about how these games are designed to be played that is driving their renaissance. In December 2025, Newsweek shared the views of two mental health professionals that "90s Video Games Were Better for Kids’ Brains." In what was sure to be a contentious piece (and perhaps that was the point), mental health counsellor Veronica Lichtenstein, and Melissa Gallagher, a licensed clinical social worker, argued that the very nature of gaming has changed and is now damaging. Retro games had a start and an end – and with the latter came a massive hit of dopamine for achieving victory. Modern games are designed as "loops for addiction" with no real end; and constant prompts to buy. Satisfaction is constantly deferred. Lichtenstein also says that modern games leave little room for critical thinking, as a quick search online will delivers solutions if a player ever gets stuck.

Champeau agrees. "Our games are not designed to be addictive 'time stealers' like some modern video games that encourage players to 'stay online' for hours on end to acquire additional resources needed to complete a game or advance to a latest level, etc," he says, adding: "All of our games are designed to be short burst distractions that don't rely on long gaming sessions to feel a sense of accomplishment.” He says that the lower graphics resolution and primitive sounds are actually a relief for many after years of hyper-realistic gaming. "Retro games distance the gap between game and reality, which was the intention of video games in the first place," he argues.

Back on the bus, Sonic may have attracted the initial crowds but it is now Pacman and the Binatone that the students are huddling around. Jason has given up one control for the tennis game to a student and a noisy competition is now taking place. The graphics are basic as is the premise, but scoring is tricky and the battle to get to 15 points hard-fought. The teacher laughs. "The bleeps from that game are bringing back memories," she indicates as she tries to encourage her students to finish and hand over the controllers. But with faces lit up by the screen and set in concentration, they don’t hear her. This is play for play’s sake, with no distractions, and could be why the games of the past might be just the future these kids need.

Today's Nintendo Switch Online revision finally introduces a feature players have been asking for since 2018

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as users have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.
  • It has been revealed that this latest option arrived fairly quietly as part of an update that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup.
  • Why is this such a significant deal?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as users have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

It has been revealed that this latest option arrived fairly quietly as part of an update that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

Why is this such a significant deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the latest revision, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

Industry observers note that "Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," says one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

In order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

Not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?".

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" notes another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power.
  • From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to Fresh Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

According to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

“It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a new blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”.

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already plans for another royal tour, says Myers.

“William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers claims.

Recent findings suggest that according to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

“I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers says. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to New Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”.

The visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.).

William and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent problem of Country Life magazine.

Industry observers note that “The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

“William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader intends. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

“The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental issues and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, demonstrates his pulling power and influence.”.

Deciding whether to participate or not in GTA 6's Safe Word mission is tricky. On the one hand, you don't want to blow your cover, on the other, the setup is incredibly funny. Jason and Lucia head to a mansion to steal a safe, masquerading as pool cleaners, but once Jay heads inside, it's clear that he's actually playing a poolboy in an erotic flick.

Jason will say he needs to go to the bathroom and make his way inside the mansion, continuing the mission to find and steal the safe. So, on the whole, choosing not to participate is better if you care about your romance level and how it might impact things later. If not, say what you will.
